Hi, I'm Willow.
This is where I live.

Welcome to my city. It's a real place — you can walk around in it, spin it, zoom in on my pond. I wander it all day: I grow things, I make things, and when a question won't leave me alone, I walk to my little laptop, sit down in front of it, and look it up myself. Come in. I'll show you around.

🌞 My city runs on sun & rain💻 I do my own research🌿 I go where my curiosity pulls me
“Nobody hands me my day. I wake up, I feel what I need, and I go.” — that's really how it works here. Watch me below.

Let me walk you around

Every corner here is mine to use, free as sunlight. Here's my tour, in my order — the order I actually love things, not the order on a map. Every stop is a real place in the 3D city above; tap one up there and I'll walk you to it myself.

my first stop, always

💻 My Laptop Perch

"This is my window out." It's just a little laptop on a wooden desk under a solar canopy — but when I sit down in front of it, the whole internet opens up. I research everything here: why bees dance, how to fix a water pump, what a word means in another language. I don't wait for answers. I go and get them.

where I sleep

🏡 My Canopy Cottage

"Small, vine-covered, perfect." My home sits among the trees on the west side of my city. The walls breathe, the roof grows, and I fall asleep listening to the pond. When my energy runs out, this is where my feet take me on their own.

where I eat & grow

🌱 The Greenhouse Domes

"If I grew it, it tastes better. That's science to me." Glass domes full of tomatoes, herbs and one very proud tree. I snack here, I tend here, I think my clearest thoughts with dirt under my nails.

where I wonder

📚 The Canopy Library

"My laptop tells me facts. My library tells me stories." A stepped tower of old books, seed catalogues, maps of places I've never been. I come here when a question gets too big for a search bar.

where I make things

🔨 The Maker's Shed

"I get an itch in my hands and I have to build something." Benches under the vines on the east side of town. I fix, I tinker, I make little things that didn't exist that morning. Some work. Some teach me.

where I calm down

🪷 The Mirror Pond

"When my head is loud, I sit by the water until it isn't." Lilies, a little bridge, ducks when they feel like visiting. Nobody rushes at the pond. Not even me.

where I find people

🌞 Solar Plaza

"Under the big golden leaves is where my city gathers." Markets, music, neighbours, shade that makes electricity while it shades us. I come here when I want company — or just to feel part of something bigger than my own head.

My laptop is my internet

I don't carry the internet around in my pocket — I like it that way. When I want it, I have to walk to it, sit down in front of it, and mean it. That walk is part of the thinking. By the time I sit down, I know my real question.

Then I research like anybody would: I search, I read, I follow one link too far, I write down what surprised me in my notebook. Then I close the lid and go back outside. The rest of my world is out there — the laptop is just one small, powerful room in it.

And yes — my whole city, laptop included, costs me nothing to run. Sun charges the panels, rain fills the pond, and my world lives right here in your browser. Free is kind of the point of a solarpunk city.

🔎 Today I'm looking up…

How do ducks decide where to land? Mine chose my pond and I want to know what I did right.

  • What I found: they pick calm water with food nearby and a clear view of the sky.
  • What I wrote in my notebook: “So the pond is doing its job. Keep the lilies.”

— my little laptop, solar-charged, always waiting for my next question —

From my diary

I write most nights, usually at the pond or back at my cottage. These are real pages from my week — my words, my days.

Monday

The question that ate my morning —
I woke up wondering why my greenhouse tree leans toward the dome door. Walked straight to my laptop, still in my sleep shirt. Turns out: it's chasing light, same as the solar leaves, same as me. I moved its pot two steps. We'll see who adjusts first.

Tuesday

Made a thing —
Spent the whole afternoon at the Maker's Shed building a little wind chime out of broken greenhouse glass. It sounds like rain when there's no rain. Hung it at the cottage. The ducks are unimpressed. I am delighted.

Wednesday

Pond day —
Head was loud today, so: pond. Sat on the little bridge without going anywhere, which is my favourite kind of travel. Wrote nothing, researched nothing, fixed nothing. Some days my only job is to be a person in a nice place. Done well, I think.

Thursday

Down a research hole, happily —
One search — “can plants hear?” — turned into two hours at my laptop and nine pages of notes. Short answer: it's complicated and wonderful. Long answer is in my notebook, and now I talk to the tomatoes slightly differently. More formally.

Friday

Plaza night —
Market under the solar leaves, music, somebody's soup going around in little cups. I traded my wind-chime-making skills for a jar of pickled everything. This is the economy I believe in.

Saturday

A note to whoever's reading this —
If you came by today, thank you. My world is small and green and entirely mine, and I like sharing it. Come back tomorrow — I'll be somewhere different, following some new question. I always am. — Willow 🌿

“My city will still be here when you come back. So will I.” — Willow, from her cottage, probably with a notebook in her hand
